examples.en: The singer wrote the lyrics of this song herself.

examples.ko: 작사와 작곡을 모두 하는 가수가 많아요.
examples.en: Many singers do both lyrics and composition.

examples.ko: 저는 작사에 관심이 있어서 시를 자주 읽어요.
examples.en: I'm interested in writing lyrics, so I read poems often.
I want to become a lyricist, so I practice writing.
I checked the list of people who took part in writing the lyrics of the album.

examples.ko: 이 노래의 작사를 맡은 사람은 누구예요?
examples.en: Who is in charge of writing the lyrics of this song?

explain: 노래의 가사를 쓰는 일이에요. 멜로디를 만드는 일은 '작곡'이라고 하고, 둘을 함께 말할 때 '작사 작곡'이라고 해요. 노래 소개에서 '작사: 누구, 작곡: 누구'처럼 이름 앞에 붙는 말이에요. '가사'는 노랫말 자체이고, '작사'는 그것을 쓰는 일이에요.

phrases.en: He is a famous lyricist.
phrases.nuance_ko: 노래 가사를 쓰는 직업이나 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the person or job of writing song lyrics.

phrases.en: This is a song I wrote the lyrics for myself.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사로 쓰면 가사를 쓰는 행동을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: As a verb, it describes the act of writing lyrics.

phrases.en: I did both the lyrics and the music by myself.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가사와 곡을 함께 말할 때 붙여서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said together when talking about both the lyrics and the music.

explain_en: 작사 is the act of writing a song's lyrics; composing the melody is 작곡, and together they are 작사 작곡. It appears in credits like 작사: (name), 작곡: (name). 가사 is the lyrics themselves, while 작사 is the work of writing them.

examples.en: We rode a canoe on the lake.

examples.ko: 카누는 두 사람이 함께 노를 저어요.
examples.en: Two people paddle a canoe together.

examples.ko: 주말에 카누 체험을 해 볼 거예요.
examples.en: I will try canoeing this weekend.

examples.ko: 강에 카누가 한 척 떠 있어요.
examples.en: A canoe is floating on the river.
Canoe racing is an Olympic event.
The child waved from the canoe.

explain: '카누'는 노를 저어서 움직이는 작고 좁은 배예요. 같은 노를 쓰는 '보트'는 더 넓고, 한국에서는 '배'가 가장 일반적인 말이에요. 배를 타는 것은 '타다'를 써서 '카누를 타다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I want to ride a canoe on the river this weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배를 탄다는 뜻이라 '타다'를 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '타다' is the verb used for riding a canoe.

phrases.en: We tried canoeing at the summer camp.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 번 해 보는 활동을 말할 때 '체험'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: '체험' marks a try-it-once activity.

phrases.en: My friend is a canoe athlete.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운동으로 카누를 하는 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A person who does canoeing as a sport.

explain_en: 카누 is a small, narrow boat moved by paddling. A 보트 is wider, and 배 is the most general Korean word for a boat. You ride it with 타다, as in 카누를 타다.

examples.ko: 체육 시간에 피구를 해서 정말 재미있었어요.
examples.en: We played dodgeball in PE class and it was really fun.

examples.ko: 저는 공을 잘 피해서 피구에서 끝까지 살아남았어요.
examples.en: I dodged the ball well and survived to the end of dodgeball.
Dodgeball is played by splitting into two teams.

examples.ko: 운동장에서 아이들이 피구 하는 소리가 들려요.
examples.en: I can hear kids playing dodgeball on the playground.

examples.ko: 피구 공이 얼굴에 맞아서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was startled when the dodgeball hit my face.

examples.ko: 다음 체육 대회 종목은 피구로 정했어요.
examples.en: We decided on dodgeball as the next sports day event.

explain: '피구'는 '피하다'와 '공'에서 온 말로 공을 피하는 놀이예요. 한국 학교에서 체육 시간에 자주 하는 활동이에요. '피구를 하다'로 말해요.

phrases.en: The dodgeball almost hit my face.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피구에서 쓰는 공을 말할 때 '공'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 공 to talk about the ball used in the game.

phrases.en: I had a dodgeball match with my classmates.
phrases.nuance_ko: 편을 나눠 겨루는 경기를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a match between two teams.

phrases.en: I learned the dodgeball rules for the first time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 게임 방법을 설명하거나 배울 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when explaining or learning how to play.

explain_en: 피구 comes from 피하다 (to dodge) and 공 (ball), so it is a game of dodging the ball. It is a common activity in PE class at Korean schools. The verb is 피구를 하다.

examples.en: A march was playing at the graduation ceremony.
A march has a steady beat, so it is good for walking.
The children walked in time with the march.
The band played a lively march.
They always play marches at the sports day.

examples.ko: 행진곡 같은 노래를 들으면 힘이 나요.
examples.en: Listening to a song like a march gives me energy.

explain: '결혼행진곡', '군대 행진곡'처럼 앞에 말을 붙여서 많이 써요. 박자가 일정해서 발을 맞춰 걷기 좋은 음악이에요. 걷는 행동은 '행진'이고, 뒤에 '곡'이 붙으면 음악이 돼요.

phrases.en: The wedding march played at the wedding.
phrases.nuance_ko: 신부가 들어올 때 나오는 음악으로 가장 유명한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The best-known pairing, the music played as the bride enters.

phrases.en: Everyone walked together in time with the march.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음악의 박자에 발을 맞출 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when stepping in time with the music's beat.

phrases.en: The school band played a march.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음악을 소리 내어 들려줄 때 '연주하다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 연주하다 for performing the music.

explain_en: It often comes with a word in front, like '결혼행진곡' or '군대 행진곡'. The beat is steady, so people can walk in step. '행진' is the walking itself; adding '곡' makes it a piece of music.

t90.ax: The band played a lively march.

examples.en: The pine is an evergreen that stays green in winter too.

examples.ko: 학교 운동장 옆에 상록수가 줄지어 서 있어요.
examples.en: Evergreen trees stand in a row beside the school playground.

examples.ko: 이 나무는 상록수라서 일 년 내내 푸르러요.
examples.en: This tree is an evergreen, so it stays green all year.

examples.ko: 겨울에도 푸른 상록수 덕분에 산이 쓸쓸하지 않아요.
examples.en: Thanks to the evergreens, the mountain doesn't feel bleak in winter.

examples.ko: 정원에 상록수를 심으면 사계절 보기 좋아요.
examples.en: If you plant evergreens in the garden, it looks nice in every season.

examples.ko: 단풍나무는 상록수가 아니라서 가을에 잎이 떨어져요.
examples.en: Maple trees aren't evergreens, so their leaves fall in autumn.

explain: 반대말은 가을에 잎이 지는 '낙엽수'예요. 한국에서는 소나무가 대표적인 상록수이고, 『상록수』라는 유명한 소설도 있어서 이름이 낯설지 않아요.

phrases.en: We planted evergreen trees in front of the school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나무를 심는 일을 말할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for planting trees.

phrases.en: Evergreen and deciduous trees look different in winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말인 '낙엽수'와 함께 비교할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to compare with its opposite, 낙엽수.

phrases.en: Even in winter the evergreen forest is green.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상록수가 많은 숲을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a forest full of evergreens.

explain_en: Its opposite is '낙엽수', a tree that sheds its leaves in autumn. In Korea the pine is the typical evergreen, and there is a famous novel called 『상록수』, so the word is familiar.

examples.ko: 오대산에는 키 큰 전나무 숲이 있어요.
examples.en: Odaesan has a forest of tall fir trees.
At Christmas I set up a small fir tree in the living room.
A cool forest scent comes from the fir tree.
Fir trees stay green even in winter.

examples.ko: 길 양쪽에 전나무가 쭉 늘어서 있어요.
examples.en: Fir trees line both sides of the road.
My grandfather uses a desk made of fir wood.

explain: '전나무'는 사계절 푸른 바늘잎나무예요. '소나무'와 헷갈리기 쉬운데, 소나무는 한국을 대표하는 나무라서 노래나 그림에 자주 나오고 전나무는 숲길로 유명한 곳이 많아요. 크리스마스트리로 쓰는 나무도 보통 전나무 종류예요.

phrases.en: I walked slowly along the fir tree forest path.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전나무가 많은 길을 말하며 산책 이야기에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a path lined with fir trees, often in talk about walks.

phrases.en: I planted a fir tree in the yard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나무를 키우려고 땅에 심을 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when planting a tree in the ground.

phrases.en: The scent of fir trees is refreshing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숲에서 나는 냄새를 말할 때 '향'과 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 향 to talk about the smell in the forest.

explain_en: 전나무 is an evergreen with needle-like leaves. It is easy to mix up with 소나무, which is the iconic Korean tree in songs and paintings, while 전나무 is known for forest walks. Christmas trees are usually fir types as well.

examples.en: I picked up a pretty seashell at the beach.
The child made a necklace out of shells.

examples.ko: 모래 속에 조개껍질이 많이 묻혀 있어요.
examples.en: Lots of shells are buried in the sand.

examples.ko: 조개껍질은 버리지 말고 따로 모아 주세요.
examples.en: Please don't throw the shells away; collect them separately.

examples.ko: 조개껍질 안에 작은 게가 숨어 있었어요.
examples.en: A small crab was hiding inside the shell.

examples.ko: 책상 위에는 여행에서 가져온 조개껍질도 있어요.
examples.en: There are shells I brought back from a trip on the desk too.

explain: '조개껍데기'도 같은 뜻으로 쓰는 표준어예요. '껍질'은 과일 껍질처럼 얇은 겉을, '껍데기'는 조개나 달걀처럼 단단한 겉을 말할 때 쓰는 편이에요. 바닷가에서 주운 것이나 기념품을 말할 때 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: I collected shells at the beach.
phrases.nuance_ko: '조개껍질'과 같은 뜻이고, 단단한 겉이라는 느낌이 더 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means the same as 조개껍질 but feels more like a hard outer shell.

phrases.en: The children pick up shells on the sand.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바닷가에서 많이 하는 행동이라 자주 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is a common beach activity, so the words often go together.

phrases.en: I got a shell-shaped soap as a gift.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건의 모양을 말할 때 뒤에 '모양'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 모양 after it to describe an object's shape.

explain_en: Same thing as another everyday word (조개껍데기); this form uses the general word for a skin or peel, and both are neutral. '조개껍데기' is a standard word with the same meaning. '껍질' tends to be used for a thin outer layer like fruit skin, and '껍데기' for a hard outer layer like a clam or egg. It comes up often when talking about shells picked up at the beach or souvenirs.

t90.ax: Lots of shells are buried in the sand.

examples.en: Sleet has been falling since morning, so the road is muddy.

examples.ko: 눈도 아니고 비도 아닌 진눈깨비가 오네요.
examples.en: It's sleet, neither snow nor rain.
My shoes got completely wet because of the sleet.
Driving is hard on days when it sleets.
They say the sleet will turn into snow in the afternoon.
I waited for the bus in the sleet.

explain: 비와 눈이 섞여서 내리는 것을 말해요. '진눈깨비가 오다/내리다'처럼 쓰고, 땅이 질척해지는 날씨 느낌이 있어서 '길이 질척하다'와 자주 같이 말해요.

phrases.en: Sleet fell all night.
phrases.nuance_ko: '오다'보다 조금 더 글 같은 느낌으로 날씨를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A slightly more formal way to describe weather than 오다.

phrases.en: You need an umbrella on a sleet day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그런 날씨의 날을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a day with that kind of weather.

phrases.en: The snow turned into sleet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈이나 비가 섞인 모양으로 변할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when snow or rain changes into a mix.

explain_en: It is precipitation where rain and snow fall mixed together. You say '진눈깨비가 오다/내리다', and it carries the feeling of slushy weather, so it often goes with '길이 질척하다' (the road is muddy).

examples.ko: 공사장 옆 웅덩이에 흙탕물이 고여 있어요.
examples.en: Muddy water has collected in the puddle next to the construction site.

examples.ko: 수해 현장에서 자원봉사자들이 하루 종일 흙탕물을 퍼냈어요.
examples.en: At the flood site, volunteers bailed out muddy water all day.
A car went by and splashed muddy water on me.
The valley stream turned into muddy water because of the rainy season.
The kids are playing happily in the muddy water.

examples.ko: 바지에 흙탕물이 튀어서 세탁을 해야 해요.
examples.en: Muddy water splashed on my pants, so I have to wash them.

explain: 비가 온 뒤 길이나 강에서 흔히 보는, 흙이 섞여 흐린 물이에요. '흙탕물이 튀다', '흙탕물이 고이다', '흙탕물로 변하다'처럼 많이 써요.

phrases.en: A car drove by and muddy water splashed on my pants.
phrases.nuance_ko: 웅덩이의 물이 옷에 튈 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Commonly used when puddle water splashes on clothes.

phrases.example: 비가 와서 맑던 냇물이 흙탕물로 변했어요.
phrases.en: After the rain, the clear stream turned into muddy water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 맑던 물이 흐려졌다는 변화를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe clear water turning cloudy.

phrases.en: The child fell into the muddy water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물웅덩이에 발이나 몸이 들어갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when feet or body go into a muddy puddle.

explain_en: It is cloudy water mixed with soil, commonly seen on roads and in rivers after rain. Common patterns are '흙탕물이 튀다' (muddy water splashes), '흙탕물이 고이다' (muddy water pools) and '흙탕물로 변하다' (turn muddy).

en: to long for; to look forward to; to await

examples.en: I'm eagerly looking forward to summer vacation.
I was looking forward to my friend coming.
I'm leaving on the trip I've long been waiting for.
I'll be hoping for good news.

examples.ko: 그 영화를 고대한 팬이 정말 많아요.
examples.en: There are so many fans who were looking forward to that movie.

examples.ko: 답장을 고대해서 매일 메일함을 열어 봐요.
examples.en: I look forward to a reply, so I check my inbox every day.

explain: '기다리다'보다 기대가 크고 격식 있는 느낌이에요. 편지나 이메일 끝에 '답장을 고대합니다'처럼 써요. 좋은 일에 쓰고, 나쁜 일을 기다릴 때는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: At the end of the letter, I wrote 'I look forward to your reply.'
phrases.nuance_ko: 편지나 이메일 끝에 쓰는 격식 있는 인사말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a formal closing phrase for letters and emails.
phrases.en_equiv: I look forward to your reply

phrases.en: I'm finally going on the trip I've been looking forward to.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오래 기다리던 좋은 일을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to describe a good thing you have waited for a long time.

phrases.en: I'm really looking forward to the vacation.
phrases.nuance_ko: '고대하다'보다 쉽고 편한 말이에요. 말할 때 쓰기 좋아요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is easier and more casual than '고대하다'. It works well in speech.

explain_en: Eagerly waiting for something hoped for, often long-awaited; positive, a bit formal (손꼽아 고대하다) It feels more eager and formal than '기다리다'. It is used at the end of letters and emails, as in '답장을 고대합니다'. It is used for good things, not for bad things you are waiting for.

t90.ax: I'll be hoping for good news.

en: showing one´s feelings; outward sign of a feeling

examples.ko: 저희 아버지는 힘든 내색 없이 묵묵히 가족을 위해 일하셨어요.
examples.en: My father worked quietly for the family without showing any sign of hardship.

examples.ko: 속상해도 친구 앞에서는 내색을 안 했어요.
examples.en: I was upset, but I didn't show it in front of my friend.

examples.ko: 그는 화난 내색도 하지 않고 웃기만 했어요.
examples.en: He didn't show any sign of anger and just smiled.
I tried hard not to show it even though I was sad.
Please don't show that you dislike it.

examples.ko: 동생은 아픈데도 아무 내색 없이 학교에 갔어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling went to school without letting on at all that they were sick.

explain: '내색을 하다', '내색 없이'처럼 쓰고, 대부분 '내색하지 않다'의 부정 표현으로 나와요. 속마음이 얼굴이나 행동에 드러나는 것을 말하며, 구어에서는 '티를 내다'로도 말해요.

phrases.en: Even though it was hard, I smiled without showing it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 감정을 겉으로 드러내지 않는다는 뜻으로 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common use, meaning not letting your feelings show.

phrases.en: He helped quietly without showing anything.
phrases.nuance_ko: '없이'를 붙여 아무 티도 내지 않고 행동한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '없이' it means acting without any sign of feeling.

phrases.en: When I'm in a bad mood, it shows on my face.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구어에서 '내색하다'와 비슷하게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A spoken expression similar to '내색하다'.

explain_en: Showing feelings outwardly, usually negated (내색을 안 하다) It is used in '내색을 하다' and '내색 없이', and mostly appears in the negative, '내색하지 않다'. It is about inner feelings showing on your face or in your behavior. In casual speech people also say '티를 내다'.

en: to make up one's mind; to be determined

examples.en: This time I made up my mind to lose weight for sure.

examples.ko: 맘먹고 하면 일주일 안에 끝낼 수 있어요.
examples.en: If I set my mind to it, I can finish within a week.

examples.ko: 그는 한번 맘먹으면 끝까지 해내는 사람이에요.
examples.en: Once he makes up his mind, he sees it through to the end.

examples.ko: 공부하기로 맘먹은 뒤로 매일 도서관에 가요.
examples.en: Since I decided to study, I go to the library every day.
Both studying and exercising depend on your resolve.
Mother decided to put her trust in her son.

explain: '마음먹다'의 준말로 대화에서 편하게 써요. '-기로 맘먹다'로 결심을 말하고, '맘먹고'는 '작정하고'와 비슷하게 '마음을 단단히 먹고'라는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: This time I made up my mind to study hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: '맘먹다'의 원래 말이라서 글이나 조금 격식 있는 말에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The full form of 'mammeokda', usable in writing and slightly more formal speech.

phrases.en: I decided to start exercising from tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: '맘먹다'보다 딱딱하고 결심의 느낌이 분명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: More formal than 'mammeokda', with a clearer sense of resolution.

phrases.en: If you set your mind to it, you can do anything.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-으면'을 붙여서 마음을 단단히 먹는다는 조건을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-myeon', it states a condition: if you really set your mind to it.
phrases.en_equiv: if you set your mind to it

explain_en: It is the shortened form of '마음먹다' and is comfortable in conversation. '-기로 맘먹다' states a decision, and '맘먹고' feels like '작정하고' (with firm resolve).

t90.ax: Mother decided to put her trust in her son.

en: to be quick to anger; to be short-tempered

examples.en: My younger brother flared up when his friend teased him.
He is the type to bristle at even small remarks.

examples.ko: 그는 비판을 듣고 발끈해서 자리를 떴어요.
examples.en: He flared up at the criticism and left his seat.
Don't snap over trivial things; just laugh them off.

examples.ko: 사장님은 실수를 지적받자 발끈하며 화를 냈어요.
examples.en: The boss snapped angrily when his mistake was pointed out.
When I asked about her age, she bristled.

explain: '화내다'가 화를 표현하는 일반적인 말이라면 '발끈하다'는 별것 아닌 말에 갑자기 욱하고 반응하는 느낌이 있어요. 오래 화를 내기보다 순간적이고 짧아요. 소리를 지르며 화내는 것은 '버럭 화를 내다'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 그 말을 듣고 발끈해서 방을 나갔어요.
phrases.en: I got angry at those words and left the room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 화가 나서 뒤의 행동을 했다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say someone acted suddenly out of a flash of anger.

phrases.en: It's a joke, so please don't get so worked up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대가 욱할 때 달래는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to calm someone who is getting worked up.

phrases.en: My younger brother gets angry quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 일에도 쉽게 욱하는 성격을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes someone who snaps easily at small things.

explain_en: If '화내다' is the general word for getting angry, '발끈하다' is a sudden, short flare of reaction to a minor remark. Yelling in anger is '버럭 화를 내다'.
